records.label: Haiyow ni / Youani / Éiouanné / Poste des Youanis
records.location_scope: Southern Choctaw country as described in the 2025 study; no coordinates assigned

documentary_references.role: Choctaw request for a post; accepted by the Trade Council on 8 February 1721 according to the study
renewed Choctaw requests for a well-stocked store
Merveilleux proposal; first mention of Haiyow ni (Youani/Éiouanné) as a possible site
Choctaw delegation and negotiations; chiefs chose a trading store in their territory and negotiated terms
scholarly source cites construction at Haiyow ni in February–March 1730 under Régis du Roullet

records.interpretation: The authors interpret the negotiations as evidence of Choctaw political agency and control over important terms of French settlement. Their suggestion that Haiyow ni was selected as the southernmost village near Mobile is explicitly speculative and is not encoded as a verified location.

records.label: Youanis (Yazoo)
records.referent_type: site named in HNOC catalogue abstract
records.location_scope: Unresolved; the HNOC abstract supplies the parenthetical '(Yazoo)'

documentary_references.role: two-page Salmon letter; original text not examined

comparisons.basis: The HNOC parenthetical '(Yazoo)' is a modern catalogue gloss. The 2025 scholarly article documents a Haiyow ni/Youanis post in southern Choctaw country but does not identify it as the site in Salmon's 1732 letter. Shared spelling alone is insufficient.
